comments.author: @altaytuna-p5q
comments.text: A huge chunk of Turkish youth, especially Millennials and Gen Z, are actually atheists, deists, or agnostics—and those numbers are growing every day. You’re even seeing a rise in Tengrists (Turkic Shamanists). Most of those secular, westernized young people you see out on the streets aren't actually Muslim. Sure, their parents and grandparents might be, but they aren't. They usually just avoid talking about religion because it’s such a touchy subject. If you put them on the spot, most will still claim to be Muslim, but it’s just a label. In reality, religion means absolutely nothing to them, and they live completely secular lives. The current conservative Turkish government is not happy about this, since they aimed to create a more religious society, but it happened the other way around! 😊

comments.text: 29:39 The fabric of Turkey has been shaped since the time of Göbeklitepe, dating back 12,000 years. The advent of early agriculture coincided with the domestication of cats; indeed, this love for cats traces its roots all the way back to that era. It would not be incorrect to say that by tracing Turkey's history, we are tracing the history of humanity itself.ıt ıs possible to witness all the stages humanity has undergone within this geography.. Stage 1: Animism and Shamanism (Göbeklitepe Period – 10,000 BC) Stage 2: Gods of Nature and Fertility (Çatalhöyük Period – 7,000 BC) Stage 3: Earthly Gods and God-Kings (Chalcolithic and Bronze Ages – 4,000 – 2,000 BC) Stage 4: Universal Monotheistic Religions (1,000 BC – 7th Century AD)....Abrahamic religions—such as Judaism, Christianity, and Islam—superseded tribal beliefs and local pantheons, establishing universal systems of law, morality, and faith that encompass all of humanity.
